summary: John's 2nd-great-grandfather; carpenter and construction superintendent of Plymouth and Wilkes-Barre who married into the Irish-Catholic Heffernans in 1892.
bio:
Addison F. Pringle was born in Plymouth; his 1943 obituary gives 2 Dec 1868, FamilySearch gives Dec 1867, the Ancestry tree screenshots show 1867 (the transcription summary says 1868), and the 1880 census age of 15 implies about 1865, so his birth year should be treated as 1865-68 with 2 Dec 1868 preferred (obituary). In June 1880 he was a 15-year-old 'laborer' in the Plymouth Twp household of his father Andrew Pringle, laborer, while his 13-year-old brother Orange was a slate picker in a coal breaker. His mother later divorced his father and resumed the name Scott; Bradsby's 1893 sketch of her lists five living children and omits Addison, then about 25 and recently married (the reason is unknown - perhaps because he lived apart from her). On 29 Jun 1892 he married Catherine E. Heffernan at Plymouth. They had eight children (Genevieve, Joseph Vincent, Mary E., Anna Theresa, Florence, Helen, Francis, Catherine). He lived in Plymouth Twp in 1900, Larksville in 1910, Wilkes-Barre Ward 15 in 1920 and at 28 Huston St, Wilkes-Barre from 1926 to 1940. The 1926 licence calls him a carpenter (born Penna). His obituary says he was a superintendent for the Ambrose West construction company and later worked at the Luzerne County Court House (as had his father-in-law Andrew H. Heffernan). He died at Wilkes-Barre on 2 Sep 1943 (PA death index 1943: 'ADDISON F PRINGLE, WLKS BRE, P652, co. 40, 9-2-43, file 82141'). The obituary names his parents as 'Andrew Pringle and Catherine Scott Pringle, early residents of the West Side' and lists 'Mrs. William Meier, Wilkes-Barre' among survivors.

The 1900 census, taken on 7 June 1900 in the East Division of Plymouth Township, gives Addison's birth as December 1867, matching the FamilySearch tree and supporting 1867 over the 1868 in his obituary ([R4-S1]). He was a carpenter, married seven years, and owned his house subject to a mortgage. The family group around him is striking: in the next dwelling lived his brother Orange Pringle (b. June 1870, a coal-breaker laborer) with their mother Catherine, recorded as 'Mother', divorced, born in May 1835 or 1838 (the last digit is unclear), mother of seven children of whom five were living; and one dwelling further on lived Ella Randal, a widow born August 1860, with her children Fred and Gertrude, very probably Addison's sister Ellen (Pringle) Randall ([R4-S1]). Three of Andrew G. Pringle's children and his former wife were thus living side by side in 1900.
funFacts: At 15 in 1880 he was already a laborer; his brother Orange, 13, picked slate in a coal breaker.

Three generations held county jobs: father-in-law Andrew H. Heffernan ('attache of the Court house'), brother-in-law Thomas F. Heffernan (assistant county treasurer), and Addison himself at the Court House.
His son Francis's 1936 marriage licence (No. 1732, Luzerne) names his parents as 'Addison F.' and 'Catherine Heffernan'.

researchLog.note: Imported from the project handoff (research rounds 1–3, Oct 2026).
Name in the Ancestry tree: "Addison F Pringle"; research uses "Addison F. Pringle".
Birth in the Ancestry tree: 2 December 1867; research: 1868-12-02.

Resolved: Why Bradsby (1893) omitted him from his mother's living children. → Not resolved directly, but the 1900 census shows he lived next door to his mother, so estrangement is unlikely; the omission is probably an error in the family-supplied sketch. In 1900 she reported 7 children born, 5 living, which matches Bradsby's 'five living' only if one of Bradsby's five was counted differently - Addison was certainly living.
Round 4 searched without result: 1943 PA death certificate #82141: not online free (Ancestry PA Death Certificates collection is paywalled)
Round 4: read the 1900 Plymouth Twp census (ED 133 sh.10B): Addison b. Dec 1867, carpenter, living next to brother Orange, divorced mother Catherine and sister Ella Randall.

conflicts.assessment: Round 4 found a different date; the tree value is kept until a certificate settles it.

Ages conflict across records: 1870 census age 5 (c.1865) and 1880 age 15 (c.1865) vs 1900 Dec 1867 vs obituary 2 Dec 1868. December is consistent; the year is 1865-68. The 1870/1880 ages were given while he was a child in his parents' household and may be more reliable than later self-reports; the 1943 death certificate is needed.
